audit.whatIsWrong: All seven phases[N].side read "Skill" while content win[0..6] read Aurora on every row — which is also exactly packet.levelChart. The full layer was the odd one out and the page rendered two answers per row.
audit.why: Both authoritative sources agree, so the stale layer is the one that moves. The kit supports an Aurora-sided lane: Malzahar has no dash or blink at any point, Malefic Visions only reaches 650, and Call of the Void matches your 900 but fires on a delay you can sidestep. His one real window is level 6, and Nether Grasp is 140 seconds at rank 1, so it does not recur often enough to own a whole stage.
audit.corrected: All seven sides set to Aurora; ratings on rows 0-3 lifted from 5/10 to 6/10 to match the rest of the chart. content win[] needed no edit. Every why rewritten so it argues the verdict its row now carries.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike ladder carried no numbers, and 'his passive shield' was treated as a timed defensive cooldown to wait out.
audit.why: Void Shift has no cooldown at all — Riot's text is 'When he hasn't recently taken damage or been crowd controlled', so it returns whenever he goes untouched. That makes it a thing you strip, not a thing you time. The real numbers are Nether Grasp 140/110/80, Call of the Void a flat 6, Malefic Visions 11 down to 7.
audit.corrected: Void Shift restated as an always-available state that one Q strips; the ladder rebuilt on the real cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page told the reader, in three separate fields, that Between Worlds dodges Nether Grasp on reaction. It also mislabelled the ultimate as a root, mislabelled Void Swarm as a shield, and called Aurora's E a 'knockback-slow'.
audit.why: The page's own breakdown.cooldowns already says 'point-and-click suppression', and enemyKit R agrees: 'channels the essence of the Void to suppress an enemy champion'. A targeted suppression at 700 cannot be reacted to with a leap, and Aurora's R has no untargetability in its text, so 'phase dodges his root on reaction' is doubly unsupported. Void Swarm is 'summons Voidlings' at 150 range — the damage reduction is Void Shift, the passive. ownerKit E damages and slows, then Aurora hops backward.
audit.corrected: Nether Grasp is now consistently a point-and-click suppression at 700 that you space rather than dodge. What Between Worlds actually does here is stated instead: its shockwave is hard CC, so it cancels a Nether Grasp channelled on someone else. Void Swarm and Void Shift are named correctly. E restated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were absent: Call of the Void silences, and Void Shift grants crowd control immunity.
audit.why: enemyKit Q flags silence, text 'silence enemy champions' at 900 range on a flat 6 seconds — that is the same range as Aurora's Q, and a silenced Aurora cannot cast the W exit the whole page is built around. enemyKit P grants 'massive damage reduction and crowd control immunity', which means Aurora's R shockwave stun does nothing at all until he has taken damage.
audit.corrected: Both are now on the page. The silence drives the trade-bad line, the don't, and the loading tips; the CC immunity drives breakdown.carry, the do, and report[5] — chip Void Shift off before your CC or your burst means anything.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit (catalogue defect 3) and told the reader to count out loud without saying what to count to.
audit.why: Nether Grasp is 140 at rank 1 and 80 at rank 3; Call of the Void is a flat 6; Void Shift has no cooldown to count at all.
audit.corrected: All three stated, including the fact that the passive is not on a timer.

audit.whatIsWrong: missingInteractions offers 'Malzahar threatens a threshold kill with Malefic Visions (E) — track the HP number, not the health bar.' I did not write it. content mid also asserted a 'flash-less all-in range'.
audit.why: Riot's Malefic Visions text is a damage-over-time that, 'If the target dies while afflicted by the visions, they pass on to a nearby enemy unit' — that is a spread-on-death, not an execute threshold, so the derived execute flag is a parsing misfire and there is no HP number to track. Whether a particular Malzahar has Flash is not knowable from any file here.
audit.corrected: Neither claim written. The Flash assertion was replaced with spacing advice keyed to the 700 range.

notes: The worst defect here was advice, not a name: three fields (late, spikes[2], wants.you[2]) told the reader that Between Worlds dodges Nether Grasp on reaction, while the page's own breakdown.cooldowns correctly called it point-and-click suppression. A player who trusts the first version dies at 6 every game. All three are now consistent with the kit, and what Aurora's R actually does in this matchup is stated instead: its shockwave is hard CC, so it cancels a Nether Grasp channelled on an ally. Two decisive interactions had never appeared anywhere on the page. Call of the Void silences at 900 — the same range as Aurora's Q — which means the W exit the whole page is built around can simply be unavailable. And Void Shift grants crowd control immunity as well as damage reduction, so Aurora's R stun does nothing until he has taken damage; that also makes Void Shift something you strip rather than something you wait out, since Riot's text gives it no cooldown at all. wants.foe[0] called it 'his Void Swarm shield' — Void Swarm summons Voidlings at 150 range; the damage reduction is the passive. content mid asserted a 'flash-less all-in range', which is not knowable from any file here, and was replaced with spacing keyed to 700. breakdown.cooldowns had no digit. I did NOT write missingInteractions' execute-threshold rule for Malefic Visions: Riot's text is a damage-over-time that passes to a nearby unit if the target dies, which is a spread-on-death, not an execute, so there is no HP number to track and the derived flag is a parsing misfire. packet.suspectNames flags 'Land Malefic Visions', 'Hit Nether Grasp' and 'Your Between Worlds' — all three are false positives where the matcher swallowed the leading verb; the ability names themselves are correct. The chart resolution here is the one I am least certain of and I have marked it Medium: full read 'Skill' on all seven rows while content and packet both read Aurora on all seven, so I moved the odd layer out, but a 50.21% win rate over 1444 games with a 7/0 chart is worth a human look — see questionsForUser.
